# Resources

Datasets, models with public code or weights, and open-source tools for ML in weather and climate.
Searchable and filterable on the site: [Datasets](https://ml4wx.github.io/datasets/) ·
[Models](https://ml4wx.github.io/models/) · [Tools](https://ml4wx.github.io/tools/). Most important first.
To add or fix one, edit or add a file in [`resources/`](../resources/) or
[suggest a resource](https://github.com/ml4wx/ml4wx.github.io/issues/new?template=resource.yml).

## Datasets (70)

### Reanalysis

| Name | What it is | Links |
|---|---|---|
| **ERA5**<br><sub>ECMWF / Copernicus C3S</sub> | ECMWF's fifth-generation global reanalysis, combining a forecast model with observations into a complete, consistent record of the atmosphere, land surface and ocean waves. It is the default training and verification target for most data-driven weather and climate models. | [site](https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/datasets/reanalysis-era5-single-levels) |
| **MERRA-2**<br><sub>NASA GMAO</sub> | NASA GMAO's global atmospheric reanalysis for the satellite era, produced with the GEOS model and including aerosol assimilation. It is a common second reanalysis for cross-checking ERA5-trained models and for aerosol and atmospheric-river studies. | [site](https://gmao.gsfc.nasa.gov/gmao-products/merra-2/) |
| **CERRA**<br><sub>Copernicus C3S (SMHI, Météo-France, MET Norway)</sub> | The Copernicus European Regional Reanalysis, a high-resolution limited-area reanalysis over Europe with a 10-member ensemble for uncertainty. It is a standard target for regional ML forecasting and downscaling over Europe. | [site](https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/datasets/reanalysis-cerra-single-levels) |
| **NCEP/NCAR Reanalysis 1**<br><sub>NOAA NCEP / NCAR</sub> | The long-running NCEP/NCAR global reanalysis (R1), still updated monthly. It is coarse and dated, but useful for long baselines and as a low-resolution reference in climate-variability and ML teaching examples. | [site](https://psl.noaa.gov/data/gridded/data.ncep.reanalysis.html) |
| **ERA5-Land**<br><sub>ECMWF / Copernicus C3S</sub> | A land-only replay of the ERA5 land component at higher resolution, giving soil moisture, snow, near-surface temperature and other land variables. ML studies use it for downscaling targets, land-surface emulation and hydrology-related forecasting. | [site](https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/datasets/reanalysis-era5-land) |
| **NOAA-CIRES-DOE 20th Century Reanalysis V3 (20CRv3)**<br><sub>NOAA PSL / CIRES / DOE</sub> | An ensemble reanalysis that assimilates only surface pressure observations, reaching back to the 19th century. ML work uses it for long training records, historical extremes and studies of data-sparse periods. | [site](https://psl.noaa.gov/data/20thC_Rean/) |
| **COSMO-REA6**<br><sub>Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD)</sub> | DWD's convection-parameterised regional reanalysis over the EURO-CORDEX domain, with hub-height wind fields. It is used for wind-energy ML, European downscaling and regional model training. | [site](https://opendata.dwd.de/climate_environment/REA/COSMO_REA6/) |
| **CERA-20C**<br><sub>ECMWF</sub> | ECMWF's coupled ocean–atmosphere reanalysis of the 20th century, run as a 10-member ensemble. It is used for long coupled training records and for studying decadal variability. | [site](https://climatedataguide.ucar.edu/climate-data/cera-20c-ecmwfs-coupled-ocean-atmosphere-reanalysis-20th-century) |
| **JRA-3Q**<br><sub>Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA)</sub> | The third Japanese global reanalysis from JMA, covering three quarters of a century. It gives an independent long reanalysis for testing how ML weather models generalise beyond ERA5. | [site](https://www.data.jma.go.jp/jra/html/JRA-3Q/index_en.html) |

### Climate model output

| Name | What it is | Links |
|---|---|---|
| **CMIP6**<br><sub>WCRP / ESGF</sub> | Phase 6 of the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project: historical, scenario and idealised simulations from dozens of climate models, distributed through ESGF. It is the main training source for climate emulators and the reference for ML-based projection and downscaling studies. | [site](https://www.wcrp-cmip.org/cmip6/) |
| **CMIP6 in the cloud (Pangeo / Google Cloud / AWS)**<br><sub>Pangeo / ESGF / LDEO</sub> | Analysis-ready Zarr copies of a large part of CMIP6, with an intake-esm catalog, hosted on public cloud buckets. ML users read it lazily with xarray instead of downloading files from ESGF. | [site](https://pangeo-data.github.io/pangeo-cmip6-cloud/) · [code](https://github.com/pangeo-data/pangeo-cmip6-cloud) ★18 |
| **NEX-GDDP-CMIP6**<br><sub>NASA Earth Exchange (NEX)</sub> | NASA's statistically downscaled and bias-corrected daily CMIP6 projections at 0.25°. It is a common baseline for ML downscaling and an input for climate-impact models. | [site](https://www.nccs.nasa.gov/services/data-collections/land-based-products/nex-gddp-cmip6) |
| **Multi-Model Large Ensemble Archive (MMLEA)**<br><sub>US CLIVAR Working Group on Large Ensembles / NCAR</sub> | A collection of initial-condition large ensembles from many climate models, remapped to a common grid. It is useful for testing whether ML emulators and detection methods hold across models. | [site](https://www.cesm.ucar.edu/community-projects/mmlea) |
| **CESM2 Large Ensemble (LENS2)**<br><sub>NCAR / IBS Center for Climate Physics</sub> | A 100-member initial-condition ensemble of CESM2 under historical and SSP3-7.0 forcing. It separates forced change from internal variability and is used to train and test climate emulators and probabilistic models. | [site](https://www.cesm.ucar.edu/community-projects/lens2) |
| **CORDEX**<br><sub>WCRP CORDEX / ESGF</sub> | WCRP's Coordinated Regional Climate Downscaling Experiment: regional climate model runs driven by global models over 14 domains. ML papers use it as training data and benchmark for learned (emulated) downscaling. | [site](https://cordex.org/) |

### Forecast archives

| Name | What it is | Links |
|---|---|---|
| **HRRR archive on AWS**<br><sub>NOAA (Zarr copy by University of Utah)</sub> | The archive of NOAA's 3 km, hourly-updated, convection-allowing High-Resolution Rapid Refresh model, with a Zarr copy. It is widely used for regional ML forecasting, downscaling and nowcasting baselines over the US. | [site](https://registry.opendata.aws/noaa-hrrr-pds/) · [code](https://github.com/blaylockbk/Herbie) ★796 |
| **ECMWF open data (IFS and AIFS real-time forecasts)**<br><sub>ECMWF</sub> | Free real-time forecasts from ECMWF's physics-based IFS (deterministic and ensemble) and its AIFS machine learning models. ML users use it to initialise models, compare against AIFS and build operational demos. | [site](https://www.ecmwf.int/en/forecasts/datasets/open-data) · [code](https://github.com/ecmwf/ecmwf-opendata) ★341 |
| **TIGGE**<br><sub>ECMWF / WMO (with CMA and NCAR)</sub> | The THORPEX Interactive Grand Global Ensemble archive of operational medium-range ensemble forecasts from many global centres. ML work uses it for multi-model post-processing and as an NWP ensemble baseline. | [site](https://confluence.ecmwf.int/display/TIGGE) |
| **S2S Prediction Project Database**<br><sub>WWRP/WCRP S2S Project, ECMWF, CMA</sub> | The WWRP/WCRP archive of subseasonal forecasts and reforecasts from operational centres, released with a 3-week delay. It is the standard NWP baseline and training source for ML subseasonal prediction. | [site](https://confluence.ecmwf.int/display/S2S) |
| **AI Weather Prediction (AIWP) model reforecasts**<br><sub>CIRA / NOAA GSL</sub> | A NOAA/CIRA archive of forecasts from FourCastNet v2, Pangu-Weather and GraphCast, each started from both GFS and IFS initial conditions. It lets researchers verify AI weather models without running them. | [site](https://registry.opendata.aws/aiwp/) |
| **NOAA GEFSv12 Reforecast**<br><sub>NOAA</sub> | Twenty years of retrospective GEFSv12 ensemble forecasts run with a fixed model version, with a matching reanalysis. It is a main training set for ML post-processing and subseasonal studies. | [site](https://registry.opendata.aws/noaa-gefs-reforecast/) |
| **C3S multi-system seasonal forecasts**<br><sub>Copernicus C3S</sub> | Copernicus seasonal forecasts and hindcasts from several European and other centres on a common grid. It is the main multi-model baseline and training source for ML seasonal prediction. | [site](https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/datasets/seasonal-original-single-levels) |

### Satellite observations

| Name | What it is | Links |
|---|---|---|
| **GPM IMERG**<br><sub>NASA GPM / GES DISC</sub> | NASA's merged multi-satellite precipitation estimate from the GPM constellation. It is a standard target for satellite-based precipitation nowcasting and for verifying ML precipitation forecasts globally. | [site](https://gpm.nasa.gov/data/imerg) |
| **Himawari-8/9 AHI on AWS**<br><sub>JMA (distributed by NOAA)</sub> | Full-disk and regional imagery from JMA's Advanced Himawari Imager, mirrored by NOAA. It is used for ML nowcasting, typhoon analysis and cloud retrievals over East Asia and the Pacific. | [site](https://registry.opendata.aws/noaa-himawari/) |
| **CERES EBAF**<br><sub>NASA LaRC</sub> | Energy-balanced top-of-atmosphere and surface radiative fluxes from NASA's CERES instruments. It is used to evaluate the radiation and cloud behaviour of ML climate emulators and hybrid models. | [site](https://ceres.larc.nasa.gov/data/) |
| **GOES-R ABI imagery on AWS**<br><sub>NOAA NESDIS</sub> | Level-1b and Level-2 products from the Advanced Baseline Imager on GOES-16 to GOES-19. It is a key input for ML nowcasting, convection detection and satellite-to-radar translation over the Americas. | [site](https://registry.opendata.aws/noaa-goes/) |
| **NCEP/CPC 4 km Merged IR (GPM_MERGIR)**<br><sub>NOAA CPC / NASA GES DISC</sub> | Half-hourly infrared brightness temperature merged from European, Japanese and US geostationary satellites. It gives a near-global, long, uniform IR record for ML convection tracking and precipitation estimation. | [site](https://disc.gsfc.nasa.gov/datasets/GPM_MERGIR_1/summary) |
| **Meteosat SEVIRI Level 1.5 (MSG 0°)**<br><sub>EUMETSAT</sub> | Rectified 12-channel imagery from the SEVIRI instrument on Meteosat Second Generation, covering Europe and Africa. It is the main geostationary input for European ML nowcasting and cloud models. | [site](https://data.eumetsat.int/product/EO:EUM:DAT:MSG:HRSEVIRI) |

| **UK Met Office NIMROD 1 km radar composite**<br><sub>UK Met Office / CEDA</sub> | The Met Office 1 km rain-rate composite of the UK radar network, archived at CEDA. It is the radar data behind well-known deep generative nowcasting work over the UK. | [site](https://catalogue.ceda.ac.uk/uuid/27dd6ffba67f667a18c62de5c3456350) |

### In-situ observations

| Name | What it is | Links |
|---|---|---|
| **NNJA (NOAA-NASA Joint Archive of Observations)**<br><sub>NOAA PSL / NASA GMAO (NNJA-AI with Brightband)</sub> | A curated archive of the conventional and satellite observations used for reanalysis, with an AI-ready Parquet version (NNJA-AI). It is the main open source of raw observations for end-to-end ML data assimilation and forecasting from observations. | [site](https://psl.noaa.gov/data/nnja_obs/) · [code](https://github.com/brightbandtech/nnja-ai) ★68 |
| **GHCN-Daily**<br><sub>NOAA NCEI</sub> | NOAA's global archive of daily station temperature, precipitation and snow. It is used to verify ML forecasts at stations and to train station-level downscaling and post-processing models. | [site](https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/products/land-based-station/global-historical-climatology-network-daily) |
| **IGRA (Integrated Global Radiosonde Archive)**<br><sub>NOAA NCEI</sub> | NOAA's global archive of radiosonde and pilot-balloon profiles. It is used to check the vertical structure of ML weather models and as upper-air input for observation-driven models. | [site](https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/products/weather-balloon/integrated-global-radiosonde-archive) |
| **HadISD**<br><sub>Met Office Hadley Centre</sub> | A quality-controlled sub-daily station dataset built from ISD by the Met Office Hadley Centre. It gives cleaner station series for training and evaluating ML models on extremes and local weather. | [site](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/hadobs/hadisd/) |
| **GHCNh (successor of ISD)**<br><sub>NOAA NCEI</sub> | NOAA's hourly and synoptic surface station dataset, which replaces the Integrated Surface Database (ISD). | **HadCRUT5**<br><sub>Met Office Hadley Centre / University of East Anglia CRU</sub> | The Met Office Hadley Centre / CRU global near-surface temperature record, given as a 200-member ensemble. | **NCEP Stage IV precipitation**<br><sub>NOAA NCEP (archived by NCAR EOL / GDEX)</sub> | The US radar–gauge multi-sensor precipitation analysis. ## Models (45)

### Global, deterministic

| Name | What it is | Links |
|---|---|---|
| **GraphCast**<br><sub>Google DeepMind</sub> | Graph neural network that steps the global atmosphere forward 6 hours at a time on a multi-scale icosahedral mesh; in the Science paper it beat ECMWF HRES on 90% of 1380 verification targets. The code now lives in the WeatherNext repo, with 0.25° (37-level and HRES-fine-tuned 13-level "operational") and 1° "small" checkpoints. | [site](https://deepmind.google/blog/graphcast-ai-model-for-faster-and-more-accurate-global-weather-forecasting/) · [code](https://github.com/google-deepmind/weathernext) ★7721 · [weights](https://console.cloud.google.com/storage/browser/dm_graphcast) |
| **AIFS Single**<br><sub>ECMWF</sub> | ECMWF's operational deterministic ML model: graph-network encoder and decoder around a sliding-window transformer, built with the open Anemoi framework. Version 2 (operational since May 2026) adds ocean-wave variables. | [site](https://huggingface.co/ecmwf/aifs-single-2.0) · [code](https://github.com/ecmwf/anemoi-core) ★170 · [weights](https://huggingface.co/ecmwf/aifs-single-2.0) |
| **Pangu-Weather**<br><sub>Huawei Cloud</sub> | 3D Earth-Specific Transformer that treats pressure levels as a third spatial dimension; four models with 1, 3, 6 and 24-hour steps are combined to limit error growth.
